claim: The Uilenspiegel Museum in Damme was renovated in 2024 and is located in the Huyse de Grote Sterre next to the town hall, with summer hours 9:30-12 and 13-17, tickets €6 (€2 reduced, €12 family).
quote: The museum, renovated in 2024, is located right next to the town hall in the Huyse de Grote Sterre, where the tourist office is also located. Summer opening hours are Monday to Sunday, 9:30am to 12pm and 1pm to 5pm. Full price is €6, reduced €2, and family tickets are €12.

claim: Damme served historically as the transhipment port of Bruges until the Zwin silted up; the Damse Vaart canal is lined with poplars over 100 years old and the Lamme Goedzak paddle steamer links Bruges' Noorweegse Kaai to Damme.
quote: This waterway features 'magnificent poplars, some of which are over 100 years old,' creating one of Belgium's most beautiful natural landscapes. The nostalgic paddle steamer Lamme Goedzak operates regular services between Bruges' Norwegian Quay and Damme.

claim: The Lamme Goedzak paddle steamer runs from 4 April to 1 November 2026, takes 35 minutes one-way, departing Bruges at 12/14/16/18h and Damme at 11/13/15/17h, with one-way tickets €12 adult / €4 child and round-trip €18 / €7.
quote: From April 4 until November 1, 2026 inclusive... From Bruges: 12:00, 14:00, 16:00, 18:00; From Damme: 11:00, 13:00, 15:00, 17:00... One-way: €12 (standard), €10 (65+), €4 (children ≤12); Round-trip: €18 (standard), €15 (65+), €7 (children ≤12)

claim: The Bruges-to-Damme cycle along the Damse Vaart is roughly four miles each way on a well-marked, easy path through Belgian countryside and along working canals.
quote: an easy, straightforward path between Damme and Bruges—about four miles each way—traversing through the Belgian countryside and along working canals

claim: Damme profiles itself as a book town with several bookshops (Boeken Diogenes, Boekhandel Maerlant, Feniks) and holds a themed book market on the second Sunday of every month, rooted in its literary heritage from Jacob Van Maerlant (13th c.) and Charles De Coster's Uilenspiegel.
quote: A themed book market takes place in Damme every second Sunday of the month... Jacob Van Maerlant, the famous southern Dutch poet, wrote his most important works here... Damme profiles itself as a book village

claim: Damme's multi-day outdoor book market for 2026 runs Thursday 14 May to Sunday 17 May, with monthly markets April-September on the square and October-March indoors in the historic town hall halls.
quote: Every second Sunday from April through September, a diverse group of booksellers gathers on the market square in Damme. Multi-day book markets are organized during May and August. Specifically for 2026, the multi-day market runs from Thursday, May 14 through Sunday, May 17, 2026.

claim: Lissewege, the 'white polder village', has been voted one of the most beautiful villages in Flanders; its 13th-century Gothic brick Onze-Lieve-Vrouw-Bezoekingkerk has a ~50 m tower built in 1265 climbable for polder views and hosts free organ concerts the last Sunday of each month.
quote: Lissewege is a charming Flemish village that 'has previously been voted one of the most beautiful villages in Flanders.'... This 13th-century Gothic brick church is the village centerpiece. Its tower, built in 1265, stands approximately 50 meters tall and offers panoramic polder views.

claim: The Ter Doest tithe barn at Lissewege dates from c.1375 and is one of the last surviving medieval tithe barns built for the maritime climate of NW Europe, measuring 50.5 m long, 23.75 m wide and 30.75 m to the gable, supported by two rows of 10 oak pillars.
quote: Dating from around 1375, this is one of the last surviving examples of a series of medieval tithe barns whose construction technique was specifically adapted to the maritime climate of north-western Europe. The barn is 50.50 m long, 23.75 m wide and the gable is 30.75 m high

claim: Ter Doest was a Cistercian abbey near Lissewege established in the 12th century, dissolved in the French Revolution in 1796; surviving on-site are the tithe barn, an octagonal chapel from 1687, a monumental porch from 1662, and an abbey farm from 1632.
quote: Beyond the iconic barn, visitors can see 'an octagonal chapel of 1687 and a monumental porch of 1662,' along with the abbey farm constructed in 1632... dissolved during the French Revolution in 1796

claim: Oostkerke Castle (Kasteel van Oostkerke) was constructed in the 14th century south of the village, rebuilt in 1938 with a Renaissance-style west wing by Baron van der Elst, and today is a private residence visible only from the public footpath.
quote: Oostkerke Castle is a castle in Damme, Belgium, constructed in the 14th century south of the village Oostkerke... Baron van der Elst had it rebuilt in 1938... Today, Oostkerke Castle is a private residence and is not open to visitors but can be easily seen from a public footpath.

claim: The Damse Vaart was commissioned in 1810 by Napoleon as part of a military supply network linking Bruges via Damme to Sluis but was never fully completed.
quote: In 1810, the Damse Vaart was commissioned by Napoleon as part of a larger network of military supply routes, though the canal was never completed as originally intended.

claim: Sint-Anna-ter-Muiden, just across the Dutch border west of Sluis, is a tiny village of a few streets that retains medieval city rights and is recommended as a detour on the Damme/Sluis cycling loop, with Hoeke sitting on the final stretch of the Damse Vaart toward Sluis.
quote: Sint-Anna-ter-Muiden, located west of Sluis, is described as charming with just a few streets and historical city rights dating back to medieval times. Hoeke is positioned in the final straight stretch toward Sluis along the Damse Vaart
